title: Nine weather patterns you can start and stop
question: Is nine the right set, and is the gap between each and the next one big enough to be worth a separate entry? Which would you cut, and what is missing?
context_md:
Every tile is the same world at the same seed, **pinned to noon** so the day/night cycle is divided out -- an earlier version left the clock running and the sun ran +0.98 on the first tile to +0.30 on the last, so BLIZZARD was dimmer than CLEAR for reasons nothing to do with weather.

600 frames per tile. The counters matter more than usual here, because **several of these are the same picture and different worlds**:

| | gusts | force | froze | bolts | ice in view | water |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLEAR | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -451 |
| BREEZE | 23 | 230 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -451 |
| GALE | 23 | **486** | 0 | 0 | 0 | -451 |
| FROST | 0 | 0 | **3844** | 0 | 20 | -1242 |
| RAIN | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **-354** |
| STORM | 23 | 410 | 0 | **1** | 0 | **-159** |
| SNOW | 0 | 0 | 15024 | 0 | 919 | -1657 |
| BLIZZARD | 23 | 463 | **29248** | 0 | **2085** | -2216 |

Three things those numbers say that the picture cannot:

- **BREEZE and GALE are identical stills** and differ 2.1x in delivered gust force. Wind is judged in motion; I can post a GIF if you want to see it.
- **FROST works and looks like it does not.** 3,844 freeze events, but the world is 8192x2560 and the frame shows 512x320 of it, so only **20** ice cells land in view. The waterline is pixel-identical to CLEAR's. That is the freeze being deliberately slow (an order of magnitude slower, at your own request) rather than broken.
- **RAIN has no lightning and STORM does**, which is the whole difference between them. `weather::strike` used to re-derive the sky from the seed and ignore a pin entirely, so a pinned storm flashed only when the seed happened to agree -- fixed here.

CLEAR is the deliberate control: it is the one entry that should move nothing.

items.label: nine pinned skies
items.caption: LIVE / CLEAR / BREEZE / GALE / FROST / RAIN / STORM / SNOW / BLIZZARD, all at noon
